blocks.text: 1. Entity Extraction
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447862863-610899086.png

Knowledge Graphs closed by pointing to entity extraction and relation extraction as the specific work of populating a graph. Entity Extraction, identifying individual entities mentioned in raw source text, is the first of those two steps, turning raw text into the nodes a graph is built from.
It scans unstructured text and pulls out the specific people, products, or organizations it actually names.
2. What Counts As An Entity
As covered generally in Knowledge Graphs, an entity is any specific, nameable thing mentioned in the text, not just any noun.
A company name or product name counts, while a generic word like product does not.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Mention","Counts as an entity"],"rows":[["Falcon Cloud","Yes, a specific, nameable company"],["the vendor","No, a generic, non-specific reference"]]}

blocks.text: 3. Tagging The Entity Type
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447862863-363189367.png
As with a schema constraining what can be expressed in Knowledge Graphs, each extracted entity is tagged with a type such as person, organization, or product.
That tag is matched against the node types the graph's schema actually allows.
4. One Mention, Many Surface Forms
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447862864-27276847.png
As with entity resolution across sources in Knowledge Graph RAG, the same real entity can appear as different surface forms across a document.
Extraction alone finds the mentions; resolving them to one entity is a separate step.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Falcon Cloud and Falcon Cloud Services referring to the same company within one document are both valid extractions from entity extraction alone; deciding they are the same entity happens in the separate entity resolution step.

blocks.text: 5. Extraction Methods Vary In Cost
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447862864-899529068.png
A simple pattern or dictionary lookup is fast but misses entities it was not told about.
A trained extraction model generalizes better but costs more to run.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Method","Tradeoff"],"rows":[["Pattern or dictionary lookup","Fast, but misses unlisted entities"],["Trained extraction model","Generalizes better, costs more to run"]]}

blocks.text: 6. Extraction Accuracy Limits The Whole Graph

blocks.alt: Extraction Accuracy Limits The Whole Graph
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447862865-653016362.png
As with an error in an early hop propagating forward in Multi-Hop RAG, a missed or wrongly typed entity here never becomes a usable graph node.
Every later step in this module depends on getting this step right first.
7. Entity Extraction Precedes Relation Extraction
Relation extraction, covered next in this module, needs already identified entities to connect together.
Entities must exist before the relationships between them can be extracted.
8. Extraction Confidence Scores
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447862865-21855744.png
As with validating arguments before executing in Tool Calling, an extracted entity often comes with a confidence score attached.
Low confidence extractions can be filtered out before they ever reach the graph.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: An entity extracted with a low confidence score should be filtered out before insertion into the graph, the same validate-before-trusting discipline as validating arguments before executing a tool call.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing When Careful Entity Extraction Is Worth The Added Effort

blocks.alt: Recognizing When Careful Entity Extraction Is Worth The Added Effort
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447862866-182229346.png
A knowledge graph meant to answer precise entity-level questions needs accurate extraction.
A rough, exploratory graph, by contrast, can tolerate a simpler, faster extraction method.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Extracting generic nouns as entities instead of specific, nameable things.
Skipping the entity type tag, leaving extracted entities unmatched to the graph schema.
Assuming extraction alone resolves different surface forms of the same entity into one.
Inserting low confidence extractions into the graph without any filtering step.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Entity extraction identifies individual entities mentioned in raw source text.
An entity is a specific, nameable thing, not just any noun in the text.
Each extracted entity is tagged with a type matching the graph schema's allowed node types.
The same real entity can appear as different surface forms; extraction finds mentions, not resolution.
Simple pattern lookups are fast but miss unlisted entities; trained models generalize but cost more.
A missed or wrongly typed entity here never becomes a usable graph node.
Relation extraction, covered next, needs already identified entities to connect together.
Extracted entities often carry a confidence score, letting low quality extractions be filtered.
Next up: Relation Extraction, covering how relationships between already identified entities are found.
